sections.h2: Which Southampton, NY office sends the tax bill?
sections.html:
The Town of Southampton Receiver of Taxes bills and collects from December 1 through May 31, and the Suffolk County Comptroller takes over after that. The Receiver's office sits on the main floor of Town Hall at 116 Hampton Road, phone 631-702-2470, with weekday counter hours of 8:30 a.m. through 4:00 p.m. The Assessor, who sets the value your bill is built on, works from the same address and answers at 631-283-6020.

Southampton is a large town on the South Fork of Long Island. The Census Bureau lists 293.5 square miles, but only 139.1 of those are land, because the Atlantic Ocean and Peconic Bay take the rest. Inside the town are seven incorporated villages (North Haven, Quogue, Sag Harbor, Sagaponack, Southampton, Westhampton Beach and West Hampton Dunes) and 16 hamlets, among them Hampton Bays, Bridgehampton, Flanders and Shinnecock Hills. If you are unsure which bill covers your address, call the Receiver before you sign a contract.

  • Receiver of Taxes: bills, receipts, duplicate bills, address changes, first-half and second-half payments.
  • Assessor: values, exemption applications, grievance forms, the tentative roll.
  • County Comptroller: every unpaid balance after May 31, plus tax liens.

sections.h2: When are Southampton property taxes due for the 2026-27 bill?
sections.html:
First-half payment is owed by January 10, 2027, and because that is a Sunday the Town moves the deadline to Monday, January 11. Second-half payment is owed by May 31, 2027. Bills go out by December 15, but the Receiver cannot mail them or take money until the Suffolk County Legislature approves the tax warrant, which usually comes after the lien date of December 1, 2026.

Not receiving a bill does not extend the penalty-free period. New York law holds the owner responsible either way, and the Town's online portal can print a duplicate bill. Mailed payments count by the USPS postmark on the envelope. A private metered postmark does not count, so send certified mail if you are near a deadline.

Southampton Receiver of Taxes calendar, 2026-27 cycle (source: Town of Southampton Important Dates page)
DateWhat happens
December 1, 2026Taxes become a lien
January 11, 2027First-half deadline (January 10 falls on a Sunday)
March 1, 2027Exemption applications due at the Assessor
March 8, 2027Notices of unpaid first-half tax mailed
May 3, 2027Second-half reminder postcards mailed
May 31, 2027Second-half deadline; later payments go to the County Comptroller

sections.h2: What does late payment cost in Southampton?
sections.html:
First-half tax paid after January 10 still goes to the Receiver, with 1 percent interest added to the base amount for each month. Anything unpaid after May 31 draws a 5 percent penalty and 5 percent interest, and the Town cannot accept those payments. They go to the County Comptroller, who adds a further 1 percent a month until the balance is cleared.

Partial payments are possible. The Receiver takes installments of at least $200 under Suffolk County Resolution 551-2001, and interest then runs only on the unpaid balance. The Comptroller also accepts partial payments on delinquent tax. The county phone for balance questions is 631-852-3000, and the Comptroller's mailing address is 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901.

  • Online: $1.75 for an ACH payment, or a 2.5 percent fee by credit card, charged by the processor and not by the Town.
  • By mail: check payable to Receiver of Taxes, drawn on a U.S. bank, or a money order.
  • A check or ACH payment returned by your bank for any reason cancels the tax payment.

sections.h2: How do I look up my Southampton tax bill and change the mailing address?
sections.html:
Use the Town's eTax portal, where the easiest search is by street address. You can also search by owner last name, tax map number or the current bill number, and no username or password is required. The record shows the owner, tax map number, zoning and taxes due. For help with the portal, the Citizens' Response Center answers at 631-702-2440 on weekdays, 8:30 a.m. onward until the 4 p.m. close.

A missing bill usually means the Town has an old mailing address. Send a change-of-address form to 116 Hampton Road, Southampton, NY 11968, fax it to 631-287-5732 or drop a copy at Town Hall. The portal's Duplicate Tax Bill option prints a fresh copy at once. Suffolk County also advises owners to tell the Assessor about any new mailing address so the roll is corrected before bills go out in December.

Before you list, pull the bill for the current year and confirm the Property Location box in the upper left corner. It carries the official street address and house number. Chapter 239 of the Southampton Town Code requires house numbers to be clearly visible from the street, a rule the Town ties to emergency response.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Southampton assessment or claim an exemption?
sections.html:
File a grievance by Grievance Day, the third Tuesday in May, which is May 18 in 2027. The Assessor's Office at Town Hall helps with the application the week before, and appointments go through 631-283-6020. The Town's tentative roll appears around May 1, so review it first. The town review board decides complaints, and it meets again off and on from June through September to work through filings.

The Town's own grievance page gives the state equalization rate and residential assessment ratio for Southampton as 59.7 percent. Keep that ratio in mind when you set your assessed value beside a sale price or appraisal.

Exemptions need an application at the Assessor by March 1. The Town lists these programs:

  • STAR and Enhanced STAR for primary residences.
  • Senior citizens.
  • Veterans.
  • Persons with disabilities and limited incomes.
  • First-time homebuyers.
  • Volunteer firefighters and ambulance workers.

Suffolk County warns that a buyer does not inherit a seller's veterans or senior exemption, so the bill can rise sharply after a sale.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Southampton tax when I sell the house?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax stays attached to the property, so it has to be settled at or before closing. Your closing attorney or title company will request a tax payoff from the Receiver before May 31, or from the County Comptroller after it. Send them the full tax-bill description of the parcel, since the Comptroller asks for it on every inquiry.

Suffolk's collection path is slower than many people expect. After May 31 the County sells a tax lien to itself, usually in the autumn or December. A one-, two- or three-family home can be redeemed within 36 months of the lien sale, other property within 12, and after that the County issues a tax deed. The Town's FAQ says the Treasurer typically starts collection on vacant land after one year and on improved property after three years of non-payment. Redemption after a deed is handled by the Suffolk Department of Planning, Division of Real Estate, at 631-853-5900.

If you paid off a mortgage during the tax year, check with the Receiver whether the bank already paid the full year. The Town notes that the bank will not necessarily forward that information, and the owner stays liable for late-payment penalties.

sections.h2: What do Southampton's numbers and climate mean for a seller?
sections.html:
Southampton homes carry high values, and the Census Bureau's 2020-2024 figures show it: homes valued at a $928,100 median, 82.4 percent of them lived in by owners, and a median household income of $128,594. Median gross rent is $2,363. The 2025 population estimate is 71,601, up from 69,036 in the 2020 census.

Weather tends to show up at inspection. NOAA normals cited by Wikipedia put Bridgehampton at about 49.8 inches of yearly precipitation and 26.8 inches of snow, and the town sits at about 26 feet above sea level on average. Buyers of waterfront and low-lying properties often ask about drainage and flood history, so gather those records before listing. The Long Island Rail Road's Montauk Branch stops in Speonk, Westhampton, Hampton Bays, Southampton and Bridgehampton.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Southampton property tax in person?
faqs.a: At the Receiver of Taxes on the main floor of Town Hall, 116 Hampton Road, weekdays between 8:30 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. Cash, checks and money orders are accepted, and you can also pay online or by mail.

faqs.q: Can I pay Southampton property tax in two parts?
faqs.a: Yes. One half is owed by January 10 (January 11 in 2027) and the other half by May 31. Smaller partial payments of at least $200 are also accepted, with interest charged only on the remaining balance.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the May 31 deadline in Southampton?
faqs.a: Payment moves to the Suffolk County Comptroller, and the balance picks up a 5 percent penalty plus interest. The Town can no longer take your payment after that date.

faqs.q: When is the Southampton exemption deadline?
faqs.a: March 1 for new or renewed exemptions, filed with the Assessor at 116 Hampton Road. Call 631-283-6020 to ask which application fits your situation.

faqs.q: Do I still owe tax if my Southampton bill never arrived?
faqs.a: Yes. Under New York law the owner is responsible for the tax whether or not a bill arrives. Ask the Receiver for a duplicate or print one from the Town's tax portal.
